Rugged tablet for PEMAC Assets Mobile (Pemac Mobile CMMS)

Pemac CMMS is cloud-based maintenance management software from Eleco Ireland (PMI Software Limited, part of Eleco plc), covering work order management, preventative maintenance, MRO inventory, calibration and compliance. The vendor targets life sciences, chemicals, healthcare, food and beverage, energy and general manufacturing, and names UK sites including Ibstock Brick and the Autolus manufacturing facility in Stevenage. The companion app is listed on Google Play as PEMAC Assets Mobile (4.4), described there as the mobile app for the PEMAC Assets CMMS maintenance server version 4.4, and on the vendor site as Pemac Mobile CMMS. The vendor says Pemac Mobile is a streamlined version of Pemac intended for use by operations personnel to request jobs and to close out work, and that mobile access is offered as part of the standard Pemac software subscription at no additional cost. The Play listing adds that users can record calibration test results, issue and receipt spare parts and enter meter readings on the plant floor.

In practice a technician walks to an asset, taps its NFC tag or scans its barcode or QR code with the device, sees the outstanding jobs for that asset, and logs the work there and then. That means the device spends its day in production areas, washdown zones and plant rooms, often in gloves and sometimes with no Wi-Fi signal. It needs an NFC radio for the tag-tapping workflow, sealing against dust and water, and a battery and screen chosen for shift work under factory lighting rather than for a sofa.

This page sets out what the vendor actually publishes about device requirements for PEMAC Assets Mobile, which Tuga device we recommend for it and why, honest notes on where the fit is unknown, generic setup steps, accessories and the questions buyers usually ask us.

Requirements

What PEMAC Assets Mobile (Pemac Mobile CMMS) needs from a device

Each item below comes from PMI Software Limited t/a Eleco Ireland (Eleco plc)'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 7.0 or later

    The Google Play listing for PEMAC Assets Mobile (4.4) (package com.pemac.pemacapp44) states the app requires Android 7.0 and up. The description text separately lists supported versions 8, 9, 10 and 11, so the vendor's own statements are not fully consistent; a device on Android 11 or later satisfies both. Source: play.google.com

  • Android or iOS only, no Windows app

    The vendor describes Pemac Mobile as an Android and iOS experience. The iOS version requires iOS 15.6 or later and supports iPhone and iPad. A Microsoft Store search returns no PEMAC products, and the vendor does not publish supported browsers or desktop system requirements. Source: pemac.com

  • Offline functionality

    The vendor states that the Pemac mobile CMMS application includes offline functionality for low- or no-bandwidth use cases and lists off-line functioning as a feature. Which modules work offline and how sync behaves are not published. Source: pemac.com

  • NFC tag reading for asset identification

    The Google Play and App Store descriptions say NFC tagging and barcode scanning are available to identify assets, spare parts and meters, and that users can find current and past jobs by tapping an NFC tag with the device. RFID is mentioned in the work orders feature list, but no UHF RFID reader support is described, so treat this as NFC tag identification unless the vendor confirms otherwise. Source: apps.apple.com

  • Barcode and QR code scanning with the device

    The vendor page lists QR code scanning and the Play listing describes barcode scanning by tapping or scanning with your device. No dedicated scan engine or Bluetooth scanner requirement is published, which implies the device camera is used. Source: play.google.com

  • Tablet or smartphone, no published hardware or screen-size guidance

    The vendor says the app is used from mobile devices like tablets and smart phones and is designed to be accessible from any device. No minimum hardware, screen size, rugged-device, scanner or NFC-reader guidance appears on pemac.com or in the store listings. The only hard requirements are the store minimums. Source: pemac.com

  • App package tied to the CMMS server version

    The current app is named PEMAC Assets Mobile (4.4) and is described as the mobile app for PEMAC Assets CMMS maintenance server version 4.4. A new package appears for each major server release, so check with your Pemac administrator which app version matches your server. Source: play.google.com

Worth knowing. We do not recommend the Tuga W10 for PEMAC Assets Mobile. The vendor describes the mobile app as Android and iOS only, a Microsoft Store search returns no PEMAC products, and the vendor does not publish supported browsers for the desktop CMMS, so we cannot confirm that it runs in a Windows browser. Two further honest caveats: the vendor publishes no screen-size, rugged-device or scanner guidance, so our device picks rest on the Android version, NFC, camera scanning and offline facts only; and the Tuga A10 and A6 scan barcodes through the camera, which depends on the app, with no dedicated scan engine. The Google Play listing also shows only 10+ downloads for the current 4.4 package, so confirm with your Pemac administrator that the app version matches your server before buying devices.
Setting up

Getting PEMAC Assets Mobile (Pemac Mobile CMMS) running

  1. Confirm with your Pemac administrator or Eleco contact which CMMS server version your site runs. The app is published per server version (currently PEMAC Assets Mobile (4.4)), and the vendor says mobile access is offered as part of the standard Pemac software subscription at no additional cost.
  2. On the Tuga A10 or A6, connect to Wi-Fi or insert a SIM, sign in with a Google account and install PEMAC Assets Mobile (4.4) from Google Play (package com.pemac.pemacapp44).
  3. Open the app and sign in with the Pemac user credentials your administrator has set up for the technician.
  4. Ask your Pemac contact how offline functionality behaves for your modules before relying on it in no-signal areas. The vendor states offline functioning is included but does not publish which screens work offline or how sync is handled.
  5. Test the workflow on one asset: tap its NFC tag with the device and, since camera scanning is app-dependent, confirm that scanning its barcode or QR code with the rear camera identifies the asset and shows its outstanding jobs.
  6. Add a charging dock for end-of-shift charging in the workshop, or a vehicle mounting dock for technicians who cover multiple sites, before rolling out to the rest of the team.
